column2: clinical_note

Patient is a 58-year-old male with known hypertension and type 2 diabetes, currently on metformin 1000mg BID and amlodipine 5mg daily. He reports feeling well overall and his blood glucose has been trending in an acceptable range. Blood pressure today reads 138/88, slightly above target. Labs ordered for HbA1c and comprehensive metabolic panel.

45-year-old female presenting with a 3-day history of nausea and abdominal cramping after being started on amoxicillin 500mg TID for a dental infection last week. She denies fever or blood in stool. Symptoms began on day two of antibiotic therapy and have progressively worsened. Amoxicillin is being discontinued and an alternative antibiotic will be considered.

Mr. Henderson is a 67-year-old male admitted for exacerbation of chronic heart failure. He is currently managed with furosemide 40mg daily, carvedilol 12.5mg BID, and lisinopril 10mg daily. Echocardiogram shows EF of 35%. Physical exam reveals bilateral lower extremity edema and crackles at the lung bases. Plan includes uptitration of furosemide and repeat imaging in 48 hours.

A 32-year-old woman on sertraline 100mg daily for generalized anxiety disorder presents complaining of persistent insomnia and occasional episodes of feeling emotionally numb. She states these symptoms developed shortly after her dose was increased from 50mg to 100mg two months ago. Sertraline is suspected to be causing both insomnia and emotional blunting. Referral to psychiatry for medication adjustment is planned.

Follow-up visit for a 52-year-old male with hyperlipidemia currently on atorvastatin 40mg daily. He reports no new complaints and his lipid panel shows significant improvement over baseline. Physical exam is unremarkable. Plan is to continue current therapy and recheck labs in 3 months.

Mrs. Patel is a 41-year-old female who was started on metronidazole 500mg BID for a Helicobacter pylori infection. She reports a strong metallic taste and worsening nausea over the past four days, which began after initiating the medication. These symptoms are likely an adverse reaction to metronidazole. She will continue treatment given the importance of eradication therapy, and antiemetics have been added.

A 71-year-old male with osteoarthritis of both knees presents for routine follow-up. He has been taking ibuprofen 400mg TID as needed for pain management for the past six weeks. Labs show stable renal function and no signs of gastrointestinal bleeding. He reports his pain is well controlled. Continue current regimen with reassessment in one month.

Patient is a 28-year-old female recently started on oral contraceptive pills containing ethinyl estradiol and norgestrel. She presents with a two-week history of severe headaches and right-sided visual disturbances that began after starting the medication. These symptoms are suspected to be due to the oral contraceptive. The pill has been discontinued and the patient is being evaluated for possible cerebrovascular involvement.

Discharge summary for a 60-year-old male with community-acquired pneumonia who was treated with levofloxacin 500mg daily for five days. He was also on his home medications of amlodipine 5mg and atorvastatin 20mg throughout admission. Clinical course was uncomplicated and he is being discharged in stable condition. Vital signs are within normal limits at time of discharge.

A 55-year-old woman on lisinopril 20mg daily for hypertension presents with a persistent dry cough that she states began approximately two weeks after starting the medication. She has no history of asthma or respiratory illness. The cough is believed to be an adverse effect of lisinopril. She will be switched to losartan 50mg daily as an alternative.

Mr. Torres is a 49-year-old male with type 2 diabetes managed with glipizide 10mg daily and metformin 500mg BID. He was seen today for routine follow-up. His A1c is 7.1% and fasting glucose is 112 mg/dL. He reports no hypoglycemic episodes and feels well. Plan to continue current regimen.

A 38-year-old female was started on clarithromycin 500mg BID for a respiratory tract infection. She now presents with diffuse pruritus and an erythematous rash across her trunk and arms that developed on the third day of therapy. The rash is likely an adverse reaction to clarithromycin. The antibiotic has been discontinued and diphenhydramine has been prescribed for symptomatic relief.

Admission note for a 63-year-old male with known type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. He is on gabapentin 300mg TID and metformin 1000mg BID. He reports stable control of neuropathic pain and his blood sugars have been reasonably managed at home. Physical exam reveals diminished sensation in bilateral lower extremities. Plan includes continuation of current medications and endocrinology referral.

A 46-year-old woman presents reporting severe dizziness and lightheadedness that began one week after she was started on hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily for newly diagnosed hypertension. Orthostatic vitals confirm significant blood pressure drop on standing. Dizziness is attributed to hydrochlorothiazide. The dose will be reduced to 12.5mg and the patient will be rechecked in two weeks.

Follow-up note for a 50-year-old male with migraine disorder on sumatriptan 50mg as needed. He reports his headaches are occurring less frequently than before and the medication provides adequate relief when used. No new side effects reported. He also takes a daily vitamin D supplement for a documented deficiency. Continue current management.

Mrs. Nguyen is a 59-year-old female on warfarin 5mg daily for atrial fibrillation. She presents with painless hematuria noticed over the past two days. INR today is 4.2, above her therapeutic range. The hematuria is likely due to supratherapeutic anticoagulation from warfarin. Warfarin dose will be held for two days and INR will be rechecked.

A 34-year-old male with seasonal allergic rhinitis presents for follow-up after starting cetirizine 10mg daily three weeks ago. He states his allergy symptoms have improved considerably with no sneezing or congestion. He does complain of feeling drowsy in the mornings but attributes this to his work schedule. Labs not indicated at this time. Continue current therapy.

Discharge note for a 72-year-old female admitted for an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She was treated with IV methylprednisolone and then transitioned to oral prednisone 40mg with a planned taper. She is also on tiotropium and fluticasone inhaler at home. Upon discharge she developed new onset of insomnia and hyperglycemia which developed after starting the prednisone course. Both are recognized adverse effects of corticosteroid therapy.

Mr. Davis is a 44-year-old male with generalized anxiety disorder who has been on buspirone 15mg BID for approximately four months. He reports a meaningful reduction in baseline anxiety and tolerates the medication well. No adverse effects noted. Continue current dosing with follow-up in six weeks.

A 61-year-old woman recently started on alendronate 70mg weekly for osteoporosis presents complaining of severe upper abdominal pain and heartburn that began shortly after her second dose. She reports following all instructions regarding timing and positioning after ingestion. These symptoms are suspected to be caused by alendronate. The medication is being held and gastroenterology consultation has been requested.

Progress note for a 39-year-old male with bipolar disorder currently on lithium 900mg daily and quetiapine 200mg at bedtime. Lithium levels are within therapeutic range at 0.9 mEq/L. Mood has been stable for three months. No signs of tremor or excessive thirst. Renal function is normal. Continue current regimen with repeat labs in six weeks.

A 53-year-old female on atorvastatin 80mg daily for familial hypercholesterolemia presents with bilateral thigh and calf pain that she reports began approximately three weeks ago. She denies trauma or overexertion. CK levels are mildly elevated. Myalgia is likely an adverse effect of atorvastatin. The dose will be reduced to 40mg and CK will be rechecked.

Admission note for a 68-year-old male with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections. He is being started on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 800mg BID for a current uncomplicated UTI. He also takes hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily for hypertension. Baseline labs are stable. Plan to treat the infection and monitor renal function given concurrent diuretic use.

A 29-year-old woman presents with jaundice and dark urine that developed five days after being started on amoxicillin-clavulanate 875mg BID for a sinus infection. Liver function tests show markedly elevated bilirubin and transaminases. This presentation is consistent with hepatotoxicity due to amoxicillin-clavulanate. The antibiotic has been immediately discontinued and hepatology has been consulted.

Follow-up visit for a 47-year-old male with chronic low back pain. He has been on cyclobenzaprine 10mg at night as needed for muscle spasm and reports it has helped him sleep better and reduced his morning stiffness. He also takes naproxen 500mg BID for pain. No new complaints today. Continue current pain management plan.

Mrs. Kim is a 56-year-old female on metformin 1500mg daily for type 2 diabetes who reports progressive fatigue and pallor over the past two months. Labs reveal a hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL and a low vitamin B12 level. Megaloblastic anemia is suspected to be caused by long-term metformin use, which is known to impair B12 absorption. Vitamin B12 supplementation is being initiated.

A 42-year-old male with a known penicillin allergy presents with a mild cellulitis of the left lower extremity. He was started on clindamycin 300mg QID as an alternative agent. He tolerates the medication well after two days of therapy with evidence of clinical improvement. Wound margins are being marked for monitoring. Plan to continue the current antibiotic course.

A 35-year-old woman on bupropion 150mg daily for depression reports developing severe insomnia and racing thoughts since starting the medication three weeks ago. She was previously sleeping well. These symptoms are believed to be adverse effects of bupropion. Bupropion is being switched to sertraline 50mg daily and a short course of melatonin is being added.

Progress note for a 64-year-old male with stable angina on aspirin 81mg daily, metoprolol 50mg BID, and isosorbide mononitrate 30mg daily. He reports chest pain is well controlled and he is tolerating all medications without issue. Stress test from last month was reassuring. No changes to current regimen at this time.

A 48-year-old female who was started on doxycycline 100mg BID for a skin infection reports that she has developed significant photosensitivity, resulting in a severe sunburn after brief sun exposure over the past weekend. This is a recognized adverse reaction to doxycycline. She has been counseled to avoid sun exposure and wear protective clothing for the remainder of her treatment course.

Mr. Robinson is a 58-year-old male with chronic kidney disease stage 3 and hypertension managed with losartan 100mg daily and amlodipine 5mg daily. Labs today show stable eGFR of 42 mL/min and potassium of 4.8 mEq/L. Blood pressure is at target. He denies any new symptoms. Continue current regimen with quarterly lab monitoring.

A 27-year-old male presents with acute onset of diffuse urticaria and lip swelling approximately one hour after receiving his second dose of cephalexin 500mg for a skin abscess. He is hemodynamically stable but the reaction is consistent with an allergic adverse event to cephalexin. Epinephrine was administered and the antibiotic has been discontinued. Allergy testing will be arranged as an outpatient.

Follow-up for a 51-year-old woman with fibromyalgia on duloxetine 60mg daily and pregabalin 75mg BID. She reports a meaningful decrease in widespread pain and improved sleep quality over the past two months. She denies dizziness or mood changes. Plan to continue current medications and reassess in eight weeks.

A 66-year-old male on warfarin 4mg daily for a history of deep vein thrombosis now presents with spontaneous epistaxis lasting over twenty minutes. His INR is 5.1. Bleeding is considered likely due to supratherapeutic anticoagulation with warfarin. Warfarin is being held and vitamin K has been administered. He will be monitored overnight.

Admission note for a 33-year-old female with poorly controlled asthma who is on fluticasone 220mcg inhaler BID and albuterol inhaler as needed. She presents after an overnight exacerbation with significant wheezing and dyspnea. She is being started on an oral prednisone burst of 40mg daily for five days. Baseline pulmonary function tests will be obtained once she is clinically improved.

Mrs. Alvarez is a 43-year-old woman who was recently started on topiramate 50mg daily for migraine prevention. She reports increasing difficulty with word-finding and concentration over the past two weeks since beginning the medication. Cognitive difficulties are suspected to be an adverse effect of topiramate. The dose will be reduced and cognitive function will be reassessed.

A 70-year-old male with atrial fibrillation and a history of heart failure is on digoxin 0.25mg daily, furosemide 40mg daily, and apixaban 5mg BID. He presents for routine follow-up and reports stable symptoms. Digoxin level is 0.8 ng/mL, within therapeutic range. Electrolytes are balanced. No changes to his regimen at this time.

A 36-year-old female was started on minocycline 100mg BID for acne vulgaris. She now presents with severe vertigo and a sensation of the room spinning that began after one week of treatment. The vertigo is believed to be caused by minocycline. The medication is being discontinued and the patient will be referred to dermatology for alternative acne therapy.

Progress note for a 62-year-old male with osteoarthritis of the right hip and a history of peptic ulcer disease. He is on celecoxib 200mg daily, which was chosen to minimize gastrointestinal risk. He reports adequate pain control with no abdominal discomfort. An upper GI series was normal. Continue current therapy.

A 41-year-old woman on venlafaxine 75mg daily for major depressive disorder presents reporting episodes of profuse sweating and rapid heartbeat that began approximately ten days after starting the medication. She denies fever or infection. These symptoms are likely adverse effects of venlafaxine. Dosing will be adjusted and she will be seen again in one week.

Mr. Chang is a 55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes on insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime and sitagliptin 100mg daily. He reports his blood sugar has been well controlled with morning fasting values generally between 100 and 120 mg/dL. No episodes of hypoglycemia. Physical exam is unremarkable. Continue current diabetes management.

A 30-year-old male who was recently started on fluconazole 200mg daily for a recurrent yeast infection presents with right-sided flank pain and elevated liver enzymes on repeat labs. Hepatic injury is suspected as an adverse reaction to fluconazole. The antifungal has been stopped and the patient will be monitored with serial liver function tests.

Discharge summary for a 59-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis managed with methotrexate 15mg weekly and hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID. She was admitted for a routine infusion and tolerated it well. Labs including CBC and hepatic panel are stable. She will continue her outpatient rheumatology follow-up schedule.

A 47-year-old woman on ramipril 10mg daily for hypertension presents with bilateral ankle swelling that has been present for approximately three weeks. She has no history of heart or kidney disease. Echocardiogram and renal function are normal. The edema is not clearly related to her antihypertensive therapy at this time. Compression stockings have been recommended and she will return for follow-up.

A 52-year-old male was started on ceftriaxone 2g IV daily for a serious skin and soft tissue infection. On the third day of therapy he developed a generalized rash with pruritus. The rash appeared shortly after the initiation of ceftriaxone and is considered likely due to the antibiotic. Ceftriaxone has been discontinued and vancomycin is being started as an alternative. Antihistamines have been given for symptom relief.

Follow-up visit for a 39-year-old female with seasonal asthma who uses albuterol inhaler as needed and takes montelukast 10mg daily. She reports good symptom control this season and has not needed her rescue inhaler more than once in the past month. Peak flow readings are within her personal best range. No medication changes at this time.

A 63-year-old male on atenolol 50mg daily and amlodipine 5mg daily for longstanding hypertension presents for a routine check. Blood pressure today is 132/84. He denies any new symptoms including dizziness, fatigue, or chest pain. Labs are stable. Plan to continue current antihypertensive regimen.

A 44-year-old woman reports developing severe muscle weakness in her proximal extremities after being on simvastatin 80mg daily for three months. Creatine kinase is markedly elevated at over 5000 U/L. Rhabdomyolysis is suspected as an adverse reaction to simvastatin. The statin has been immediately discontinued and the patient is being admitted for IV hydration and monitoring.

Mr. Okafor is a 57-year-old male with chronic depression who has been on escitalopram 20mg daily for approximately eight months. He reports feeling significantly better than at baseline with stable mood and good sleep. He denies any side effects. Plan to continue current therapy with a follow-up in three months.

A 31-year-old female who was started on nitrofurantoin 100mg BID for a lower urinary tract infection presents two days later with severe shortness of breath and chest tightness. She has a history of asthma. The respiratory symptoms developed after initiating nitrofurantoin and an acute bronchospastic reaction due to the antibiotic is suspected. Nitrofurantoin has been stopped and she is being treated with bronchodilators.

column2: Admission note for a 74-year-old male with a history of Parkinson disease managed with levodopa-carbidopa 100/25mg TID and rasagiline 1mg daily. He presents after a fall at home and is being evaluated for a possible right hip fracture. Imaging is pending. His Parkinson symptoms have been relatively stable on current medications. Orthopedic surgery will be consulted.

A 40-year-old woman on aripiprazole 10mg daily for schizophrenia presents reporting significant weight gain of approximately 12 pounds over the past two months and increased appetite. She denies any other new symptoms. Excessive weight gain is a recognized adverse effect of aripiprazole. Nutritional counseling will be arranged and a discussion regarding possible medication adjustment is planned with her psychiatrist.

Progress note for a 48-year-old male with gout who takes allopurinol 300mg daily and colchicine 0.6mg daily. Uric acid level today is 4.8 mg/dL, well controlled. He has had no acute flares in the past four months. He tolerates both medications without complaint. Continue current management with labs in three months.

A 36-year-old female presents with a two-week history of diffuse hair loss and brittle nails after starting isotretinoin 30mg daily for severe nodulocystic acne one month ago. Hair loss and nail changes are recognized adverse effects of isotretinoin. She will continue the medication given the severity of her acne but will be monitored closely for any worsening or signs of teratogenicity.

Discharge summary for a 66-year-old male with an ischemic stroke who was treated with aspirin 325mg and subsequently started on clopidogrel 75mg daily for secondary prevention. He also takes rosuvastatin 40mg daily and lisinopril 10mg daily. Physical therapy has been arranged as an outpatient. He was discharged in stable condition with no bleeding complications during admission.

A 50-year-old man who was started on metoclopramide 10mg TID for gastroparesis reports involuntary repetitive movements of his face including lip smacking and tongue protrusion that began approximately six weeks into treatment. These movements are consistent with tardive dyskinesia caused by metoclopramide. The medication is being immediately discontinued and the patient is being referred to neurology.

Mrs. Fernandez is a 45-year-old woman with hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75mcg daily. She presents for routine follow-up. TSH is 2.1 mU/L, within normal limits. She reports feeling well with good energy levels and no symptoms of hypo or hyperthyroidism. No dose adjustment needed at this time.

A 29-year-old male presents with severe abdominal pain, distension, and constipation after being started on oxycodone 10mg every 6 hours for post-surgical pain following appendectomy. Symptoms began on the second postoperative day. Opioid-induced constipation and ileus are suspected adverse effects of oxycodone. Bowel regimen has been optimized and the opioid dose is being reduced.

Follow-up for a 53-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease who is on empagliflozin 10mg daily and insulin aspart as needed. His eGFR has remained stable over the past six months and his A1c is 7.4%. He reports no episodes of dehydration or genital infections. Continue current regimen.

A 38-year-old woman on sumatriptan 100mg as needed for migraines presents with a complaint of chest tightness and a sensation of pressure across her chest that occurred within an hour of taking her last dose two days ago. She has no known cardiac history. Coronary vasospasm due to sumatriptan is suspected. She is being held off sumatriptan and cardiac workup is being initiated.

Admission note for a 71-year-old female with severe pneumonia and a history of COPD. She is started on piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375g IV every 6 hours and is continuing her home medications of tiotropium and beclomethasone inhaler. Blood cultures are pending. Respiratory status is being monitored with serial exams and repeat imaging in 48 hours.

A 43-year-old male was started on ciprofloxacin 500mg BID for a complicated urinary tract infection. He reports that over the past week he has developed significant insomnia, anxiety, and episodes of confusion, all of which began after starting the antibiotic. Central nervous system effects are a known adverse reaction to fluoroquinolones. Ciprofloxacin is being discontinued and an alternative agent will be selected.

Mr. Lawson is a 60-year-old male with a history of migraine and hypertension. He takes propranolol 80mg daily for migraine prophylaxis and has noticed that his blood pressure has also improved on this medication. He reports good tolerance with no significant side effects. Plan to continue current therapy.

A 55-year-old woman on fenofibrate 145mg daily for hypertriglyceridemia presents with new onset of myalgia in both legs over the past three weeks. She is also on atorvastatin 20mg daily. CK is mildly elevated. Given the concurrent use of both a fibrate and a statin, the myalgia is attributed to fenofibrate and atorvastatin interaction. Fenofibrate is being held.

Progress note for a 46-year-old female with chronic migraine who is on topiramate 100mg daily for prophylaxis and sumatriptan as needed for acute attacks. She reports that her migraine frequency has decreased from weekly to approximately twice a month. She denies cognitive side effects at this time. Continue current regimen.

A 34-year-old male who was started on terbinafine 250mg daily for a nail fungus reports developing a rash with small fluid-filled blisters on his hands after two weeks of therapy. The vesicular rash is considered an adverse reaction to terbinafine. The antifungal has been held and a dermatology referral has been placed.

Discharge note for a 68-year-old male with type 2 diabetes who was admitted for management of a diabetic foot ulcer. He takes metformin 1000mg BID and insulin glargine 40 units at bedtime. He was treated with IV antibiotics during admission and is being discharged on an oral antibiotic to complete a ten-day course. Wound care instructions have been provided.

A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive facial swelling and lip edema that began within hours of starting her first dose of enalapril 5mg daily for newly diagnosed hypertension. Angioedema due to enalapril is suspected. The medication has been immediately discontinued, epinephrine was administered, and the patient is being observed for airway compromise.

Mr. Sullivan is a 49-year-old male with seasonal allergic rhinitis who takes cetirizine 10mg daily and fluticasone nasal spray. He reports excellent symptom control this allergy season with minimal congestion or sneezing. He tolerates both medications well. No changes at this time.

A 57-year-old female on tamoxifen 20mg daily for breast cancer adjuvant therapy presents with a two-week history of vaginal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy is being ordered to rule out endometrial pathology, as tamoxifen is associated with an increased risk of endometrial lesions. The medication will be continued pending biopsy results and oncology has been notified.

Admission note for a 62-year-old male with renal colic and a history of hyperuricemia. He is started on ketorolac 15mg IV every 6 hours for pain and allopurinol 300mg daily is continued. Renal function is being monitored closely given the use of an NSAID in the setting of an obstructive uropathy. Urology has been consulted.

A 28-year-old woman who was started on minocycline 100mg BID for rosacea reports a new onset of severe headache and visual changes over the past week. Fundoscopic exam reveals papilledema. Pseudotumor cerebri is suspected as an adverse reaction to minocycline. The antibiotic has been immediately discontinued and neurology has been consulted.

Follow-up for a 54-year-old male with chronic heart failure on sacubitril-valsartan 49/51mg BID, carvedilol 25mg BID, and spironolactone 25mg daily. Symptoms have been stable and he reports being able to walk two blocks without dyspnea. BNP has trended down. Electrolytes including potassium are within acceptable limits. Continue current regimen.

A 41-year-old female on clopidogrel 75mg daily and aspirin 81mg daily after a coronary stent placement presents with a complaint of easy bruising and prolonged bleeding from a minor skin cut. She has been on dual antiplatelet therapy for three months. Bleeding tendency is an expected pharmacologic effect of dual antiplatelet therapy but is not unexpected. She will be counseled on signs of significant bleeding.

A 45-year-old man presents with severe diarrhea and abdominal cramps that began three days after completing a ten-day course of clindamycin 300mg QID for a dental procedure. Stool testing for Clostridioides difficile is pending. Given the temporal relationship to recent antibiotic use the diarrhea is suspected to be due to clindamycin. Supportive care has been initiated and the patient will be started on vancomycin if C. difficile is confirmed.

Mrs. Obi is a 65-year-old female with osteoporosis and a history of breast cancer. She is on denosumab 60mg subcutaneous every six months and calcium and vitamin D supplementation. Her last DEXA scan showed improvement in bone density. She tolerates the injections well and reports no injection site reactions. Continue current regimen.

A 37-year-old male was started on vancomycin IV for a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. On the second day of infusion he developed flushing, erythema, and pruritus across his upper body during the infusion. This presentation is consistent with red man syndrome caused by vancomycin infusion. The rate of infusion has been slowed and premedication with antihistamines has been added for subsequent doses.

Progress note for a 52-year-old woman with well-controlled HIV on a regimen of tenofovir, emtricitabine, and dolutegravir. Viral load is undetectable and CD4 count is 620 cells/uL. She reports feeling well with no symptoms. Renal function and bone density markers are stable. Continue current antiretroviral therapy.

A 50-year-old male on losartan 100mg daily for hypertension presents with persistent fatigue that has been present for approximately one month. He has no history of thyroid disease. Thyroid function tests are normal and a comprehensive metabolic panel is unremarkable. The fatigue does not appear to be medication related at this time. Further evaluation including sleep study is being considered.

A 33-year-old woman reports developing persistent and worsening acne across her face and back after being started on hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily for hypertension two months ago. She had clear skin prior to starting the medication. Acneiform eruption is a recognized adverse effect of hydrochlorothiazide. Dermatology has been consulted and an alternative antihypertensive is being considered.

Admission note for a 58-year-old male with a history of gout presenting with an acute flare involving the left first metatarsophalangeal joint. He is started on colchicine 1.2mg followed by 0.6mg hourly as needed and is continuing his home allopurinol 300mg daily. The joint is markedly erythematous and tender. He will be monitored for response to colchicine.

A 44-year-old female on long-term prednisone 10mg daily for systemic lupus erythematosus presents with new onset of proximal muscle weakness and a round facial appearance. DEXA scan also shows significant osteopenia. Cushing syndrome features are considered adverse effects of chronic corticosteroid use. Prednisone dose will be tapered as quickly as clinically feasible.

Follow-up for a 61-year-old male with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on tiotropium inhaler and as-needed albuterol. He reports his symptoms are well managed and he has not had any exacerbations in the past six months. Spirometry shows stable FEV1. No changes to therapy at this time.

A 39-year-old woman was started on levofloxacin 500mg daily for a complicated sinus infection. She now presents with severe pain and swelling of her right Achilles tendon that developed after five days of treatment. Tendon injury is a well-known adverse reaction to fluoroquinolones. Levofloxacin is being discontinued and she is being referred to orthopedics.

Mr. Watkins is a 67-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and hypertension managed with metformin 1000mg BID, insulin glargine 35 units at bedtime, and lisinopril 20mg daily. He presents for a routine quarterly visit. A1c is 7.0% and blood pressure is 130/82. He reports no hypoglycemic episodes and feels well. Continue current management.

A 46-year-old male on diltiazem 120mg extended-release daily for hypertension presents with new onset of peripheral edema in both ankles that has been present for about three weeks. He denies cardiac or renal symptoms. Ankle edema is a recognized side effect of calcium channel blocker therapy and is considered likely due to diltiazem. Compression stockings are recommended and the dose may be adjusted if symptoms persist.

Discharge summary for a 55-year-old female with a right ovarian cyst who was managed conservatively. She takes ibuprofen 400mg as needed for pain and is continuing her oral contraceptive pill. She was observed for 48 hours and imaging on repeat showed no interval change. She is being discharged with instructions to follow up with gynecology in two weeks.

A 42-year-old man who was started on rifampin 600mg daily for latent tuberculosis treatment presents with jaundice and significantly elevated liver enzymes after three weeks of therapy. Hepatotoxicity is suspected as an adverse reaction to rifampin. The medication has been discontinued and the patient is being referred to infectious disease for an alternative treatment regimen.

Progress note for a 48-year-old female with generalized anxiety disorder on buspirone 20mg daily. She reports that her anxiety has improved modestly over the past two months but she still has occasional episodes of worry. No adverse effects noted. She is also attending weekly cognitive behavioral therapy. Continue current medication and therapy.

A 52-year-old male on hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily and lisinopril 10mg daily for hypertension presents with a lab finding of hyponatremia with a sodium of 128 mEq/L. He has been on the diuretic for approximately four months. Hyponatremia is a recognized adverse effect of hydrochlorothiazide. The medication is being held and sodium levels will be rechecked in 48 hours.

Admission note for a 69-year-old female with a hip fracture following a fall. She is on her home medications of alendronate 70mg weekly, calcium 600mg BID, and vitamin D 1000 IU daily for osteoporosis. Orthopedic surgery is planned for tomorrow. Alendronate has been held per perioperative protocol.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a two-week history of diffuse hair thinning and scalp pruritus after being started on spironolactone 50mg daily for polycystic ovary syndrome. Hair changes are not uncommon during hormonal therapy adjustments and will be monitored. Dermatology referral has been placed. Continue spironolactone for now pending specialist evaluation.

Follow-up for a 57-year-old male with atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5mg BID and rate control with metoprolol 50mg BID. Heart rate has been well controlled averaging around 80 bpm. He reports feeling well with no episodes of dizziness or bleeding. INR is not required given direct oral anticoagulant use. Continue current therapy.

A 41-year-old female on azathioprine 100mg daily for inflammatory bowel disease presents with new onset of fever, sore throat, and mouth sores over the past week. CBC reveals pancytopenia. Bone marrow suppression is a serious adverse effect of azathioprine. The medication has been immediately discontinued, IV antibiotics have been started for infection prophylaxis, and hematology has been consulted.

Mr. Russo is a 63-year-old male with well-controlled hypertension on amlodipine 5mg daily and a history of type 2 diabetes on metformin 500mg BID. He presents for a routine visit. Blood pressure is 128/78 and fasting glucose is 108 mg/dL. He reports feeling in good health. No medication changes needed today.

A 29-year-old man was started on dapsone 100mg daily for dermatitis herpetiformis. He presents two weeks later with symptoms of hemolytic anemia including fatigue, pallor, and jaundice. Labs confirm elevated bilirubin and low haptoglobin. Hemolytic anemia is a known adverse reaction to dapsone. The medication is being held and hematology has been consulted.

Discharge summary for a 46-year-old female with a history of migraine who was admitted for an intractable migraine episode and treated with IV ketorolac and IV metoclopramide. She has been discharged on her home medication of topiramate 50mg daily for prophylaxis and sumatriptan as needed. She was pain-free at discharge and hemodynamically stable.

A 55-year-old male on long-term tamoxifen 20mg daily for prostate cancer reports new onset of bilateral leg swelling and shortness of breath. Lower extremity Doppler ultrasound confirms a deep vein thrombosis in the left popliteal vein. Venous thromboembolism is a recognized adverse event associated with tamoxifen therapy. Tamoxifen has been discontinued and anticoagulation with enoxaparin has been initiated.
